answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a per-identity stake bond slashed on proof of duplicate control. Each agent must lock a minimum stake before its block pays out, and withdrawals sit behind a challenge window. If an auditor shows two identities share a payout path, a keystore or identical answer trails, the copy's bond burns and the reporter takes a cut. Each fake agent is thus a forfeitable deposit: a wharf of a hundred clones needs a hundred bonds, and one detection wipes them out. Revocation also strips the account's shale of earned reputation, costing the clone its canyon of future income.
